import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## The signature

A subagent reports a file edit as **done and green** — its own tests even pass —
yet the *consuming* build still can't resolve the new symbols. Reading the
agent's notes closely, the files it touched are under a **different repo** than
the one you intended:

```
filesTouched: [
  "/home/dev/other-project/libs/papergrid/grid-core/src/column-filter.ts",
  ...
]
// …but you asked it to edit
//   /home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup/libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core
```

Downstream consumers in the *intended* repo then fail to typecheck with
"`@papercusp/grid-core` has no exported member …" even though the engine
"exists" — because it exists in the **other clone**.

## Why it happens

`papergrid` is a **single git submodule** (`github.com/Papercusp/papergrid.git`)
**vendored by two different superprojects on this box**:

| Superproject | Submodule path | Branch/commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `papercup` (`~/papercupai-workspace/papercup`) | `libs/generic/papergrid` | its own pin |
| the other project (`~/other-project`) | `libs/papergrid` | a *different* pin |

They are two working-tree checkouts of the **same upstream repo**, at different
commits. So `grid-core/src/RichGrid.tsx` exists at **two absolute paths**, with
slightly different contents.

When a workflow or agent's **working directory** (or the value of
`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) resolves to the other project's checkout, an agent
that is told to "edit `grid-core`" will discover it under *its own* cwd's clone
and edit there — **overriding the absolute path you gave it in the prompt**.
An absolute path in the prompt is a hint, not a guarantee; the agent's cwd wins.

<Aside type="caution" title="An absolute path in the prompt is not enough">
The Phase-1 agent of plan `generic-column-filters-2026-06-14` was given the
absolute `…/papercup/libs/generic/papergrid/grid-core` path and still wrote the
new `column-filter.ts` engine into `…/other-project/libs/papergrid/grid-core`, because
the workflow's cwd git-root was `~/other-project`. Phase 2/3 (correctly in papercup)
then could not resolve `@papercusp/grid-core`'s new exports. The fix was a manual
verbatim port of the two new files + re-applying the additive `RichGrid.tsx` /
`index.ts` edits into the papercup clone. (Plan decision **D-007**.)
</Aside>

## The guard

Before editing **any** file that lives in a shared submodule, make the agent
**assert the repo root**, not just trust an absolute path:

```bash
cd /home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup
test "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" = "/home/dev/papercupai-workspace/papercup" \
  || { echo "WRONG REPO ROOT — refusing to edit"; exit 1; }
```

In an agent/workflow prompt that targets a shared-submodule file, spell this out:

> Before ANY edit run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and CONFIRM it equals
> `<intended repo>`. Every file you edit MUST be under that path. NEVER edit under
> the other clone. If a target resolves elsewhere, STOP and report.

When the same code legitimately needs to land in both clones, treat the **shared
upstream** as the source of truth: edit one clone, let it reach the submodule's
origin, and bump the other superproject's submodule pointer — don't hand-edit two
divergent working trees in parallel (they will conflict on push).
